residual_risk: Not provable in-tree: the first real trusted-publisher publish. Every check here is structural or stubbed; the OIDC exchange only happens on a v* tag against npmjs.com.

Dropping setup-node's registry-url is the judgement call. npm's own example keeps it, but it exists solely to wire NODE_AUTH_TOKEN; without it no .npmrc is written and the OIDC exchange starts from a clean, unauthenticated npm. If the next release fails on auth, re-adding `registry-url: https://registry.npmjs.org` is the first thing to try.
`npm install -g npm@latest` is unpinned, so a broken npm release breaks a release. The version assert right after it names the floor but not a ceiling.
The trusted publisher is bound to the filename release.yml. Nothing in CI can detect a rename; only docs/releasing.md warns about it.
Network was unavailable in this session, so npm's docs could not be re-read — the 22.14 / 11.5.1 floors are the ones the task body states.

results.summary:
release.yml now publishes through npm's trusted publisher: no NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, no secrets.* expression, and no setup-node registry-url (that option only exists to write an .npmrc reading NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, which would hand npm a half-written auth line to start the OIDC exchange from). A new `runner` step runs `npm install -g npm@latest` and then asserts node >= 22.14 and npm >= 11.5.1 — the floors npm documents for trusted publishing; Node 22 still bundles npm 10, and an npm that quietly stayed there fails at publish time as "need auth", pointing at a token that no longer exists. `id-token: write` and `--provenance --access public` are unchanged.

The fork degrade is now identity rather than secret presence: the `preflight` step publishes only when GITHUB_REPOSITORY equals the repository package.json already names, so the upstream is written down once and a rename cannot leave a stale literal behind. A fork gets a ::notice:: naming both repositories and the fix, and the run stays green.

docs/releasing.md leads with the tag (the operator's only step) and gains a section recording the four trusted-publisher fields, since they live in npmjs.com's settings and a failing publish has nothing in-tree to read otherwise. Two consequences are called out for whoever next refactors CI: the workflow FILENAME is part of the trusted-publisher identity — renaming release.yml or moving the publish step into another workflow breaks releases until npmjs.com is updated — and a fork can never publish hkb-cli. Troubleshooting gained an authentication case that points at the trusted publisher, not at a missing secret.

test/release.test.js had to follow (it asserts on release.yml's parsed structure and on docs/releasing.md, so it would otherwise fail); it is outside the task's declared paths but is the test for the two files the task owns.

Draft PR #63. Still on the operator: revoke the npm bypass token and delete the NPM_TOKEN repo secret — the workflow already ignores both, so the order does not matter. The end-to-end proof of "Done when" is the next v* tag publishing with provenance and zero secrets.
